claims.statement: Every business Bundle roots its code at cn.shopex.ecshopx.<domain> and follows a standard package skeleton: api/admin/v1 and api/front/v1 (+ api/open for callbacks) controllers, service, domain entities, mapper interfaces, dispatch job handlers and event listeners, cron Schedule*Handler classes, port interfaces the Bundle owns, integration implementations of other Bundles' Ports, config, and an optional repository layer; orders, goods, members, and kaquan all follow it, though not every Bundle carries every package (kaquan has no repository/, members has no cron/, goods' cron/ holds only the test-cron mock config).

Controllers are split by API surface: api/admin/v1 controllers carry @AdminAuth (plus @ShopLog) and map /api/v1 or /api/v1/<domain>; api/front/v1 controllers carry @FrontAuth or @FrontNoAuth and always map under /api/v1/h5app, with Mini Program endpoints further namespaced by wxapp; api/open holds unauthenticated callbacks and legacy PHP-URL-compatibility routes such as the WeChat Pay notify endpoint at /wechatAuth/wxpay/notify. The public Open API is served by the dedicated ecshopx-openapi module at /api/openapi/internal/v1|v2 plus a catch-all gateway at /api/openapi, not from business-Bundle api/ packages.

Every controller passes an explicit bean name to @RestController to avoid collisions in the single Spring context that scans cn.shopex.ecshopx.**: the dominant pattern is <domain><Surface>V1<Entity> (ordersAdminV1Order, ordersFrontV1WxappPayment, goodsAdminV1Items, membersFrontV1Members) while kaquan uses the variant <domain><Entity><Surface>V1 (kaquanVipGradeAdminV1, kaquanDiscountCardFrontV1), and the openapi module uses openapiV1*/openapiV2* names.

Mapper bean-name collisions across Bundles are prevented not by manual names but by FqcnMapperBeanNameGenerator, installed by EcshopxApplication via @MapperScan(basePackages = cn.shopex.ecshopx.**.mapper, nameGenerator = FqcnMapperBeanNameGenerator.class, sqlSessionFactoryRef = sqlSessionFactory, lazyInitialization = true); a mapper interface only works if it lives in a mapper package, and its XML only loads via mybatis-plus.mapper-locations=classpath*:mapper/**/*.xml in the bootstrap application.properties.

Write-side service logic in mature Bundles follows a responsibility split: a @Service RequestGate (e.g. DistributorCreateRequestGate) re-reads the operator JWT, enforces menu-permission route aliases, asserts company activation, and narrows entity scope, throwing Unauthorized/BadRequest/Forbidden before business code runs; a stateless ParamValidator with static validate(Map) checks field shape; and an Orchestrator (DistributorCreateOrchestrator) owns @Transactional(rollbackFor = Exception.class), sequences duplicate checks, third-party guard clients, the delegated insert, and registers a TransactionSynchronization whose afterCommit publishes the dispatch job and event in fixed order.

port/ holds interfaces this Bundle owns that other Bundles implement (e.g. orders/port/WxappCartAddPort, whose Javadoc states it is implemented by the goods module to avoid an orders-to-goods dependency, with the implementation at goods/service/cart/wxapp/WxappCartAddPortImpl injected by orders' CartController), while integration/ holds this Bundle's implementations of Ports owned by other Bundles; most shared Port interfaces live in ecshopx-common under common/port/<domain>/ so consumers never depend on providers, which keeps the peer graph acyclic (goods depends on orders, never the reverse).

orders/integration/JushuitanSettingReadPortImpl implements common/port/order/JushuitanSettingReadPort by delegating to the orders-local OrdersErpSettingRedisReadService, letting aftersales and system-link consume the same Port without depending on ecshopx-orders; likewise each Bundle's openapi/ package (e.g. orders/openapi/OpenapiOrderListPortImpl implementing common/openapi/OpenapiOrderListPort) adapts the Bundle to the ecshopx-openapi gateway, which itself depends only on ecshopx-common.

dispatch/ beans come in two shapes implementing interfaces from ecshopx-common: *JobHandler implements DispatchHandler with handle(Map) (e.g. FinishOrderJobHandler normalizing null payload to Map.of() and delegating to FinishOrderJobService) and *DispatchListener implements DispatchListener with onEvent(Map) (e.g. UpdateItemSalesDispatchListener on EVENT_TRADE_FINISH); they are never registered by annotation — ecshopx-bootstrap contains explicit *RegistrationConfig @Configuration classes that call dispatchRegistry.registerJob/registerEventListener in @PostConstruct, and DispatchBusConfig instantiates the DispatchRegistry, DispatchFacade, and the sync/Redis drivers.

Publisher-side dispatch interfaces (FinishOrderJobDispatchPublisher, OrdersTradeFinishDispatchPublisher, DistributionAddEventDispatchPublisher, …) live in ecshopx-common so a Bundle can publish without depending on the bus implementation or the consumer; their DispatchFacade-backed implementations are provided by ecshopx-bootstrap (e.g. FinishOrderJobDispatchPublisherImpl dispatches with ASYNC/REDIS/slow options), and after-commit semantics are provided either inline via TransactionSynchronizationManager in the orchestrator or via a dedicated *AfterCommitDispatchPublisher wrapper bean registered @Primary in the bootstrap.

cron/ holds XXL-JOB handlers named Schedule*Handler that are pure delegators: a @Component with a @XxlJob(short-name) method that times the call, logs done/failed in the [cron][<name>] shape with cost in ms, delegates to a service, and on exception publishes a CronAlertEvent via ApplicationEventPublisher and rethrows so XXL-JOB marks the run failed; orders has 18 such handlers and kaquan's ScheduleCancelExpiredCardHandler follows the same pattern, and the contract is pinned by per-handler tests asserting the log shape and the alert-and-rethrow behaviour.

Every business Bundle's POM depends on ecshopx-common (most add ecshopx-dispatch) plus a curated set of peer Bundles it actually needs; ecshopx-orders lists work-wechat, third-party, supplier, reservation, espier, members, companys, point, aftersales, payment, chinaums-pay, deposit, hfpay, popularize, and super-admin, while ecshopx-bootstrap depends on every Bundle, is the only module with the spring-boot-maven-plugin (mainClass cn.shopex.ecshopx.EcshopxApplication), and carries the Flyway migrations, the global application.properties, and the dispatch-bus and registration configuration.

domain/ entities are annotated with the extended MyBatis-Plus metadata annotations @MpTable/@MpId/@MpField/@MpIndex from common/mybatis/metadata, which are meta-annotated with the stock @TableName/@TableId/@TableField and additionally carry column type, length, nullability, comments, and indexes migrated from the legacy Doctrine ORM; the bin/make-migration helper diffs the live MySQL schema against these domains to generate Flyway SQL under ecshopx-bootstrap/src/main/resources/db/migration, and the readme requires manually reviewing the generated SQL for types, defaults, NULL allowance, comments, and indexes.

repository/ is an optional @Repository layer composing mapper calls into named operations (orders/repository/CategoryTaxRateRepository wraps CategoryTaxRateMapper with findDuplicateForCreate, insertEntity, updateByIdPartialReturningRow owning the MyBatis-Plus wrapper logic); simple flows may call the mappers directly, as FinishOrderBatchService does with NormalOrdersMapper.

Bundle-scoped @RestControllerAdvice classes are tightly scoped to one API surface rather than global: orders/config/OrdersAdminV1ExceptionAdvice uses basePackages = cn.shopex.ecshopx.orders.api.admin.v1 and maps BadRequest/Resource exceptions to a Dingo-style 200-with-data envelope, while kaquan's DiscountCardControllerExceptionAdvice lives next to the controllers in api/admin/v1 and scopes by assignableTypes; both are ordered @Order(HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE).

event/ and listener/ form a lighter third async mechanism distinct from the dispatch bus and cron: plain Spring ApplicationEvents (PaySuccessSpringEvent, NormalOrderCancelSpringEvent, OrderProcessLogSpringEvent) consumed by @TransactionalEventListener(phase = AFTER_COMMIT, fallbackExecution = true) beans such as orders/listener/OrderProcessLogSpringEventListener, used for intra-Bundle after-commit work that does not need retry or cross-Bundle fan-out.

config/ holds Bundle-local Spring beans (e.g. orders/config/OrdersSchedulingConfig with @EnableScheduling, executor configs, and the scoped advice classes), and the cron/testcfg/CronTestMockConfig class in src/main (not src/test) is annotated @Profile(test-cron) to swap side-effect beans such as dispatch publishers, Redis writes, and third-party ports for No-op implementations during cron-diff testing.

When a Port implementation would otherwise create a dependency cycle, ecshopx-bootstrap supplies the adapter itself: e.g. bootstrap/order/CompanyPassportUidByCompanyIdPortAdapter implements common/port/companys/CompanyPassportUidByCompanyIdPort by delegating to CompanysMapper, sitting alongside the bootstrap's many cn.shopex.ecshopx.config.*RegistrationConfig and *DispatchPublisherImpl classes that wire cross-Bundle jobs and events.
